evidence: The supplied issue context identifies issue #51 with a non-empty bug title, detailed reproduction, expected behavior, evidence, and impact.

src/workflows/work-on.ts:641-667 constructs an ActiveRunLink with subagentRunId `pending:${runId}`, activeNodes `{}`, and currentNodeId `resolve-1`, then persists it before awaiting #dispatchNode.

src/workflows/work-on.ts:1729-1931 shows that node.queued, the durable launch-intent node.started event, provider spawn, and receipt binding all happen only after that initial pending link has been published to session state.

src/workflows/orchestrate.ts:449-463 treats any matching listRuns() entry as an existing started child without validating its receipt, and src/workflows/orchestrate.ts:516-523 writes that value directly into lane.started.

src/workflows/work-on.ts:297-305 sends link.subagentRunId to provider status unless isLaunchSentinel returns true, while src/workflows/work-on.ts:3692-3694 recognizes only `launch:` values; therefore a restored `pending:` bootstrap value is queried as a provider run ID.

src/index.ts:14-17 attaches the orchestration lifecycle listener before controller restart reconciliation and resumes orchestration afterward, permitting the pending-link failure lifecycle and lane resumption paths to race around the same restored bootstrap record.

src/workflows/work-on.ts:3578-3620 accepts any string subagentRunId when restoring a link and preserves an explicitly empty activeNodes object, so the bootstrap placeholder remains untyped and unrecoverable.

Supplied production evidence records lane.started with `pending:ed9d9544-8f29-4bf4-bba7-95eae63cb74f`, followed by lane.needs-human after `Async run not found`, while the Forge snapshot remained active with no nodes.
